title: Computer will not power on
question: Does it show any charging or power indicator?
steps: Inspect a known-good outlet, approved adapter, cable and charge indicators; use the OEM power-reset instructions.
command: No software command applies before power/POST.
expected: Indicators or POST separate power-source faults from firmware/display faults.
branches: Yes: inspect display/POST; no: isolate supply/battery and escalate hardware.
safety: No battery opening or firmware flashing. Stop for swelling, heat, liquid damage.

title: Computer powers on but has no display
question: Does a known-good external display show firmware or Windows?
steps: Check brightness/output selection and a known-good monitor/cable; record OEM POST indicators.
command: No invasive command; compare external display behavior.
expected: External display works: investigate panel/output; neither works: inspect POST/hardware.
branches: POST reached: boot workflow; no POST: OEM hardware diagnostic/support.
safety: Do not dismantle damaged equipment or guess firmware changes.

title: Computer will not boot Windows
question: Does firmware detect the intended internal disk?
steps: Inspect firmware boot menu; boot trusted recovery; identify disks/volumes and encryption before repair.
command: diskpart → list disk → list volume → exit (inspection only)
expected: A positively identified Windows installation and system partition, or evidence of missing/failing storage.
branches: Disk absent/errors: data preservation; disk present/unlocked: recovery and boot-configuration procedure.
safety: Never format or assume Disk 0/C: in recovery.

title: Blue screen or repeated crashes
question: Is the same stop code or failure repeated after a recent change?
steps: Record time/stop code; inventory dumps; correlate driver changes and hardware health.
expected: Dump timestamps correlate with the symptom; debugger output needs context.
branches: Repeatable driver path: vendor-compatible rollback after approval; hardware errors: memory/storage diagnosis.
safety: Dumps may contain sensitive data; do not copy or publish by default.

title: Computer running slowly
question: Is the slowdown linked to one workload or resource?
steps: Use Process Explorer CPU/memory/disk observations and relevant events; collect PerfView trace only with scope.
expected: Resource or timing evidence tied to the actual workload.
branches: Single app: software workflow; broad resource pressure: storage/memory/startup investigation.
safety: Do not terminate unknown processes or disable security/startup indiscriminately.

title: Overheating
question: Does heat correlate with fan/airflow or a particular workload?
steps: Inspect vents/fan behavior and HWiNFO sensors at idle and the actual approved workload.
command: Open HWiNFO Sensors; record temperature and fan behavior.
expected: Stable idle/workload readings, or thermal shutdown/throttling evidence.
branches: Thermal issue: OEM cleaning/service; normal readings: investigate power or crashes.
safety: Do not burn-in unstable equipment or set arbitrary unsafe temperature limits.

title: Hard drive or SSD failure
question: Are there I/O errors, disappearing storage or abnormal noises?
steps: Inspect CrystalDiskInfo and existing SMART tools; stop repeated reads/writes on failing media.
command: smartctl.exe --scan-open (authorized device discovery; choose the correct reported device)
expected: Identified device and health evidence; SMART does not certify reliability.
branches: Failure suspected: separate-storage image/specialist recovery; healthy evidence: filesystem/OS investigation.
safety: Do not run write-heavy CHKDSK repair, benchmarks or partition edits on a failing drive.

title: Deleted or inaccessible files
question: Is data deleted, encrypted, blocked by permissions or on failing media?
steps: Stop writes to the source; identify encryption/health; use a copy/image for TestDisk, PhotoRec or DMDE investigation.
command: Get-Acl -LiteralPath "C:\ApprovedPath" (replace with the authorized actual path)
expected: Permission evidence or recoverable file candidates without source modifications.
branches: Permissions: targeted ACL procedure; deletion: recover to another disk; encrypted: legitimate key recovery.
safety: Do not restore recovered files onto the source disk or change broad ownership.

title: Windows password or account access problem
question: Which identity type and exact error are involved?
steps: Check keyboard/layout, connectivity, lockout timing and owner-authorized account recovery.
command: Open Settings > Accounts; collect the exact error without passwords.
expected: Correct identity/recovery route identified.
branches: Local/Microsoft: official owner recovery; AD/Entra: authorized administrator and audit process.
safety: No offline SAM edits, password-removal tools or credential bypass.

title: BitLocker recovery screen
question: Can the owner/admin retrieve the key matching the displayed key ID?
steps: Record key ID only, identify the encrypted target and use the authorized owner/directory recovery channel.
expected: Volume, protection and lock state; no recovery secret in the report.
branches: Key available: owner enters it in the recovery UI; no key: stop and escalate.
safety: Never store the 48-digit password in toolkit logs, command history or reports.

title: No internet
question: Does the adapter have a valid link, address and default gateway?
steps: Run existing general/connectivity diagnostics; compare a known-good client on the same network.
expected: Interface, addressing, gateway and DNS show the failing layer.
branches: No link: physical/adapter; bad address: DHCP; good gateway: DNS/transport/application.
safety: Do not reset the network or disable firewall by default.

title: Wi-Fi connected but internet unavailable
question: Can the device reach its configured gateway?
steps: Run Wi-Fi and connectivity scripts; check captive portal, addressing and DNS separately.
expected: Wireless link state is separated from gateway/DNS/HTTPS evidence.
branches: Gateway fails: wireless/network path; gateway works: DNS/proxy/captive portal/upstream.
safety: Do not export wireless passwords or change enterprise Wi-Fi profiles blindly.

title: DNS resolution failure
question: Is the intended name failing only on this device or resolver?
steps: Run the DNS script; compare configured resolver and expected organizational suffix.
command: Resolve-DnsName -Name example.com -Type A -DnsOnly (public example; use an authorized real name)
expected: Records or specific DNS error; distinguish timeout from no-such-name.
branches: All names fail: resolver/path; one name fails: record/suffix/application investigation.
safety: Do not substitute public DNS on a domain endpoint without approval.

title: DHCP address failure
question: Is the address self-assigned or the lease/gateway unexpected?
steps: Run DHCP diagnostics; inspect link/VLAN and compare a known-good endpoint.
expected: Lease/address/gateway evidence or self-assigned addressing.
branches: Link good/no lease: DHCP/VLAN administrator; correct lease: routing/DNS workflow.
safety: Release/renew can end remote access; arrange a recovery path first.

title: Network connection slow or unstable
question: Is the issue local link, packet loss, congestion or the application?
steps: Inspect link and error behavior; use iperf3 only with an authorized known peer and capture scope.
command: iperf3.exe --version (read-only dependency check; throughput test needs an approved server)
expected: Tool version and a planned scoped peer test, not an unsolicited scan.
branches: Local peer slow: link/Wi-Fi; local good/upstream slow: gateway/VPN/provider/application.
safety: Scans and captures require permitted targets; captures can contain sensitive data.

title: Windows Update failure
question: What update/error code and servicing/reboot state are involved?
steps: Collect filtered WindowsUpdateClient events, free space and DISM health evidence before remediation.
expected: Health state and relevant servicing/update errors.
branches: Corruption: planned compatible-source servicing; policy/network issue: enterprise diagnostics.
safety: Do not delete update stores or reset components automatically.

title: Application will not install
question: Is the package trusted, compatible and blocked by context/dependencies?
steps: Inspect Orca tables if MSI; record version/signature and installer error/log.
command: msiexec.exe /? (help only; /i and /x are target modifications)
expected: Applicable options and exact error; 1603 needs log investigation, 1618 concurrent install, 3010 reboot required.
branches: Dependency/context: correct approved prerequisites; unsupported package: vendor/admin escalation.
safety: Do not patch signed vendor MSI or accept license terms silently.

title: Application crashes
question: Does it fail for one user, one data file or every launch?
steps: Correlate Application events, dumps, app version/dependencies and a safe alternate user/test input.
expected: Time-linked application error, not automatic proof of a named module root cause.
branches: One profile/data input: profile/application-data investigation; all users: package/dependency/vendor.
safety: Preserve user data and dumps; do not reinstall or delete app settings before backup.

title: Missing or malfunctioning drivers
question: What device ID, error and signed OEM version are involved?
steps: Open Device Manager; run existing driver inventory and preserve driver backup.
expected: Exact device/version/signature evidence for a compatible OEM package.
branches: Known regression: approved rollback; missing package: official exact-model driver.
safety: No random driver updater or ForceUnsigned.

title: USB device not recognized
question: Does the same device work on a known-good port/cable/PC?
steps: Use USB Device Tree Viewer and USBDeview; compare known-good physical combinations.
command: Open Device Manager > device Properties > General and Details > Hardware Ids.
expected: Topology/device error differentiates port, cable, device and driver.
branches: Fails across known-good devices: hardware; specific host: driver/controller/power investigation.
safety: Do not remove unrelated device history or flash firmware as an initial test.

title: Printer not working
question: Is the intended printer reachable and the queue/spooler healthy?
steps: Inspect Settings printers, intended port/driver, spooler state and relevant queue errors.
expected: Service status compared with intended printer/queue evidence.
branches: Stopped service: identify cause before approved restart; wrong port/driver: controlled correction.
safety: Do not purge other users' jobs or delete spool files indiscriminately.

title: Suspected malware
question: Is there credible evidence and an active incident/retention requirement?
steps: Follow incident procedure; record time and indicators; inspect Defender and persistence read-only; apply report hold.
expected: Protection state and preserved evidence, not a clean-system certificate.
branches: Credible compromise: authorized incident team/isolation; uncertain indicator: scoped evidence collection.
safety: Do not disable security, clear logs, delete persistence/evidence or publish captured data.

title: Domain sign-in failure
question: Are organization DNS, time and domain-controller connectivity correct?
steps: Inspect gpresult, clock and domain membership; query secure-channel status without repair.
expected: Time source/state correlated with DNS, account error and join status.
branches: Lockout: administrator procedure; DNS/time: correct approved environment; trust issue: scoped admin recovery.
safety: No automatic domain removal/rejoin, account reset or security weakening.

title: Entra device-registration issue
question: Does actual join/user state match the intended tenant and deployment?
steps: Collect dsregcmd status in the affected user context and compare registration/policy/network/time evidence.
expected: Join/registration evidence; one field does not prove all SSO works.
branches: Wrong context: retest intended user; registration/enrollment issue: tenant administrator.
safety: Do not run dsregcmd /leave or re-enroll automatically.

title: Corrupt Windows user profile
question: Does another authorized test profile work and are files backed up?
steps: Preserve affected data; inspect User Profile Service events; distinguish account, storage and profile fault.
command: Open Event Viewer: right-click Start > Event Viewer > Windows Logs > Application.
expected: Profile-specific evidence and independent verified data backup.
branches: Storage/account problem: relevant procedure; profile-only: approved replacement profile and selective migration.
safety: Do not delete profile folders, alter ProfileList or reset credentials blindly.

title: New PC setup and deployment
question: Are hardware, license, organization enrollment and backup requirements known?
steps: Complete deployment intake; verify media/drivers/licenses and test planned settings on disposable compatible hardware.
expected: Correct client/build/architecture for the intended licensed deployment.
branches: Managed target: approved enrollment/provisioning; personal target: licensed official setup plan.
safety: Image apply, partition work and provisioning are separate approved changes, never menu tests.

title: Migrating an old PC to a new PC
question: Is ordinary file copy sufficient or is supported user-state migration required?
steps: Inventory data/cloud/EFS/apps; verify separate protected backup; preview selected file scope; test restore.
expected: Explicit scope, capacity and a new independent destination; no apps/credentials migrated by file-copy wrapper.
branches: Ordinary files: reviewed copy/verification; supported client state: reviewed elevated USMT; Entra/server: approved alternative.
safety: No destructive mirror/move, existing destination merge or unprotected secret storage.
